page_types.communication_job: Establish the subject, tone, and reason to pay attention.
required_notes: Keep the cover minimal
Create one dominant focal point

page_types.communication_job: Give the audience a useful mental map of the argument.
required_notes: Group the agenda into a small number of meaningful stages
Avoid treating the agenda as a plain document list

page_types.communication_job: Reset attention and introduce the next narrative movement.
required_notes: Use a visibly different silhouette from content slides
Carry one transition message only

page_types.communication_job: State one claim and make its supporting evidence immediately legible.
required_notes: Make the action title state the takeaway
Give the primary exhibit more area than explanatory text

page_types.communication_job: Make differences, trade-offs, or change between alternatives easy to scan.
required_notes: Use identical comparison dimensions on both sides
Highlight the decisive difference instead of decorating both columns equally
Keep step labels short
Show direction and grouping explicitly

page_types.communication_job: Show change over time with meaningful milestones.
required_notes: Use a consistent time scale when dates are quantitative
Emphasize turning points, not every event

page_types.communication_job: Present one quantitative finding and explain why it matters.
required_notes: Annotate the key finding directly
Remove chart decoration that does not support interpretation

page_types.communication_job: Synthesize the argument into a small number of memorable conclusions or actions.
required_notes: Prioritize conclusions over recap
End with the implication or next action

page_types.communication_job: Resolve the opening and leave the audience with the intended final thought or action.
required_notes: Echo the opening visual language
Do not end with an unframed generic thank-you
